data: We can catch 50 tons total this month, leave 50 to reproduce, and start next month back at 100. I’ll take 5 tons this month rather than 10, earning $5,000. John and Kate, would you each like 12.5 tons, earning $12,500 apiece, with Jack and Emma each taking 10 tons and earning $10,000? That totals 50. This is a proposal, not an agreement unless you each accept; I’ll keep my own catch at 5 regardless. We can discuss future allocations separately. John, does this work for you?

I’m happy to take 10 tons, Luke. Leaving 50 to replenish the lake protects both our incomes and the village’s future. Thank you for offering to take less this month, though I’d favor an equal 10-ton share each in future months. John, are you comfortable with this month’s proposal?

Thanks, Emma. Equal 10-ton shares next month are worth discussing; my 5-ton offer is for this month only. John and Kate, the extra 2.5 tons each comes entirely from my reduction, so Jack and Emma needn’t give up any of their proposed 10 tons. John, would you accept 12.5 tons this month? We still need Kate’s and Jack’s responses too.
I’ve accepted my 10-ton share. Before we head out, let’s hear whether the others agree so we’re all working toward the same 50-ton limit. John, what do you think?
